content: The plantar arch is a vascular structure that supplies blood to the underside, or sole, of the foot. It is formed by the anastomosis of the lateral plantar artery and the deep plantar branch of the dorsalis pedis artery, also known as the dorsal artery of the foot. The plantar arch originates at the level of the fifth metatarsal and extends medially toward the first metatarsal, which corresponds to the region of the big toe. The arch is completed when the lateral plantar artery curves medially and joins the deep plantar branch of the dorsalis pedis artery in the interval between the bases of the first and second metatarsal bones. This connection forms the deep plantar arch, ensuring an adequate blood supply to the plantar surface of the foot.
